summary: Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a master's course at Kyoto University around 1964–1966. He served as an assistant professor at Tokai University (~1985–2007) and president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).

Nobuyuki Yamagiwa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He taught Shayne Clarke, held a lecturer post at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002), and is attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1960–1969) under Issai Funahashi and doctoral supervisor Genjun Sasaki, later working there as an assistant, lecturer, and Buddhist studies research room appointee (~1970–2006).

Nolan Pliny Jacobson was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Emory University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. He taught at several institutions and was Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Winthrop University (1954–1974).

Noopur Shalini works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at NIFT, IGNOU, Ningbo University, and the University of Mumbai, she held an archaeology post at Zhejiang University in 2023.

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1911–1914). She held posts at the University of St Andrews and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).

Norbert M. Samuelson was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned degrees from Northwestern, HUC-JIR, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He held major posts at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University.

Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi, later serving as a longtime professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011).

Noriaki Hosoda is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He held assistant and associate professor posts at Hokkaido University (attested 1986 and 2003) and is attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University until 1953. He is attested as a professor at Taisho University in 1982.

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He had a long academic career at Bukkyo University, rising from lecturer in 1976 to professor and later professor emeritus (2015–2021).
Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He is attested as an assistant at the Osaka University of Foreign Studies in 1962.
Norihiro Matsuura is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Matsuura is attested in 2026 as faculty at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Norihisa Baba is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He has served as a professor at the University of Tokyo and its Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. Koyama is attested as head of the Matsunami Seiren Sensei Koki Kinenkai (2007) and professor at Taisho University (2014).

Noritoshi Aramaki is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He taught numerous scholars and held posts as associate professor and professor at Kyoto University, associate professor at Osaka University, and professor at Otani University.

Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Bukkyo University. He has held teaching posts at Bukkyo University and Soka University, including its International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.

Norman Brooke Jopson was a linguistics and Indology scholar educated at Cambridge, Vienna (under Paul Kretschmer), Charles University, and Saint Petersburg. He held posts as Reader at King's College London and Professor of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1937–1955).

Norman Cutler was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Michigan, Washington, and the University of Chicago under A. K. Ramanujan. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Chicago from around 1979 to 2002.

Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure educated at Colgate, Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union. He studied under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, and founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.
